{{Short description|Algebraic geometry surface, studied by Julius Plücker (1899)}}
{{For|the hypersurface parameterizing lines in 3-space, also sometimes called a Plücker surface|Plücker coordinates}}

In [[algebraic geometry]], a '''Plücker surface''', studied by {{harvs|txt|authorlink=Julius Plücker|first=Julius |last=Plücker|year=1899}}, is a [[quartic surface]] in 3-dimensional [[projective space]] with a double line and 8 nodes.

==Construction==
For any [[quadric line complex]], the lines of the complex in a plane envelop a quadric in the plane. A Plücker surface
depends on the choice of a quadric line complex and a line, and consists of points of the quadrics associated to  the planes through the chosen line.<ref>{{Citation | authorlink=R. W. H. T. Hudson | last1=Hudson | first1=R. W. H. T. | title=Kummer's quartic surface | page=68 | publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] | series=Cambridge Mathematical Library | isbn=978-0-521-39790-2 | mr=1097176  | year=1990|url=https://archive.org/details/184605691}}</ref>
